title: The Rule of 72: How Time Multiplies Your Money
hook_text: YOUR MONEY IS DOUBLING RIGHT NOW

beats.say: Here's the math banks don't want you to calculate.
beats.visual: A cinematic shot of a dark room with a single desk lamp illuminating a stack of coins, moody shadows, 35mm film.

beats.say: It's called the Rule of 72, and it explains how wealth actually builds.
beats.visual: Close-up of a vintage metallic clock ticking slowly, blurred background, warm tungsten lighting, cinematic depth of field.

beats.say: Divide 72 by your investment return, and you get the years it takes to double.
beats.visual: A sleek fountain pen resting on a blank parchment notebook, overhead shot, soft natural window light.

beats.say: At 8% a year, your money doubles every 9 years without extra work.
beats.visual: Macro shot of a tiny green seedling pushing through dark soil, soft morning sun rays, moody atmosphere.

beats.say: Start at 25 investing $200 a month at 8%, and you reach $698,202 by 65.
beats.visual: A vintage leather briefcase resting on a wooden floor by a large factory window, dust motes in sunbeams.

beats.say: Wait until 35 with that exact same plan, and you drop to $298,072.
beats.visual: A hand placing a single chess piece on a dark wooden board, cinematic sidelight, shallow focus.

beats.say: That ten-year delay costs you $400,130 in final wealth.
beats.visual: A rusty iron key lying on a concrete slab, cold industrial lighting, minimalist framing.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions. The rule works against debt too.
beats.visual: A dark hallway with a single flickering overhead light bulb casting long shadows on brick walls.

beats.say: At 24% credit card APR, debt doubles every 3 years.
beats.visual: Macro shot of a red warning light pulsing slowly in a dark server room, high contrast.

beats.say: A $6,000 balance paid with minimums turns into 21 years and $10,887 in interest.
beats.visual: An old mechanical calculator on a metal desk, numbers rolling on paper tape, moody film grain.

beats.say: Time is the hidden multiplier of everything you own or owe.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person walking away down a long concrete pier at dusk, horizon glowing orange.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A sleek dark fountain pen drawing a sharp straight line on heavy paper, dramatic studio lighting.

caption: Time is your greatest asset or your worst enemy. The math doesn't care about your intentions. #personalfinance #investing #moneytips #wealthbuilding #finance
description: Discover how the Rule of 72 dictates the speed of your wealth and your debt. A step-by-step breakdown of how a ten-year delay alters your financial future.
first_comment: Did you start investing in your 20s or wait until later? Let's talk numbers below.

facts.claim: $200/month invested for 40 years at 8%/yr (monthly compounding) = $698,202 (you put in $96,000)
$200/month invested for 20 years at 8%/yr (monthly compounding) = $117,804 (you put in $48,000)
Starting at 25 vs 35 with $200/month at 8% until 65: $698,202 vs $298,072 (10 years late costs $400,130)
Rule of 72: at 8% money doubles every 9 years; at 24% debt doubles every 3 years
$6,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum (1% + interest, min $25): 252 months (~21 years), $10,887 interest
